We attempted apply_template with the original SMILES (with atom mapping) but got empty result '()'. Possibly need to use unmapped SMILES (canonical). The template is a retrosynthetic transformation: product -> precursors. The product is the molecule given. The template's retro_smarts: product side is left side? Actually retro_smarts_template: '[C:8]-[C@@H;D3;+0:9]...>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])... .[C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10]...'. So applying retro template to product yields two fragments: one is carbonyl fragment (C=O etc) and the other is an alkene fragment.

Thus applying template to product should give list of precursor SMILES strings: likely something like "C=O fragment" and "alkene fragment". Let's try apply_template with canonical SMILES (without mapping) we attempted and got error due to stereochemistry. Maybe need to provide SMILES without stereochemistry? The product SMILES: "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F". That is the product? Actually the product is the given initial molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... etc). That's same as "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F". The error came from rdkit assigning stereochemistry on None. Possibly need to include explicit stereochemistry? The template expects certain stereochemistry. Maybe we need to use the mapped SMILES as product? The first apply_template with mapped SMILES gave empty result, meaning no match.

Maybe the template expects product with certain stereochemistry (C@H etc). Our product is maybe missing chiral tags. The mapped_rxn shows product side: ([CH3:1][C@H:2]... etc). So product has chiral centers. Our SMILES "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F" lacks stereochemistry. So need to provide SMILES with stereochemistry matching template. The product in mapped_rxn: [CH3:1][C@H:2]... So the product is a chiral center at C2 (attached to CH3, aromatic, etc). Also C9 is chiral? The product includes [C@@H:9]1... etc. So we need to supply SMILES with stereochemistry: maybe "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F"? Wait the product has a CH3 attached to chiral carbon? The mapped_rxn product: [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1... )... So carbon 2 attached to CH3, aromatic ring, and rest of chain. So product SMILES: "CC(C1=...?)" Actually CH3 attached to chiral carbon which also attached to aromatic ring and to the rest of chain (C@@H:9...). The chain includes a cyclobutane? Let's reconstruct: product: [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]. So carbon 2 attached to CH3, aromatic phenyl, and carbon 9 (which is part of a cyclobutane?). Carbon 9 is chiral attached to carbon 2, CH2 chain, and carbon 13 (which has OH and CF3). So product is a bicyclic? Hard.

But maybe we can still apply template using the mapped product SMILES: "[CH3][C@H]([c]1... )...". Let's try using the mapped product SMILES from mapped_rxn product side: " [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]". Remove atom map numbers. So SMILES: "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CC C[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)F"? Need correct. Let's construct: CH3 = C, chiral carbon with H: [C@H] attached to aromatic phenyl (c1ccccc1) and to the cyclobutane chain. So SMILES: "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F"? That matches earlier but with stereochemistry: "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F". Also need stereochemistry at the other chiral center: the carbon in the cyclobutane attached to OH and CF3 is [C@@] maybe? The SMILES "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F" does not specify stereochemistry for that carbon. Could add [C@@] but not sure.

Let's try apply_template with SMILES "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F".
